newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index ends up for fourth straight session.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index ends up for fourth straight session.

text.p: ** Shares record hectic gains, firm mood
** Bombay 30-share index jumps 1.60 pct to 3,413.41
provisional close, off 3,443.56--day's high
** Foreign funds and speculators among major buyers
** All-round market optimism helps market rally, as small
investors jump in to buy stocks--traders
** Top gainers include ITC, L&T, Tata Tea and Hindalco
** National exchange index advances 2.39 pct to 979.45
provisional

A sustained buying interest in front-bencher stocks by foreign funds coupled with fresh bidding in the broader market helped Bombay shares on Friday to close higher for the fourth consecutive session, dealers sid.
A sharp rise in pivotals as well as second-tier stocks led to an overall optimistic picture being painted in the market.
"There is a growing feeling among fund managers not to get left behind in the rally," said institutional dealer Govind Agarwal at local brokerage Motilal Oswal.
Bombay stocks have surged five percent this week on market hopes about government policies to revive capital markets.
The policy package which is due in mid-January is expected to boost industrial growth and revive sagging capital markets.
Sharp price movements in small cap stocks was a pointer to improved liquidity and a lot of demand being generated in the market, traders said.
"Retail investors are also showing interest...follow-up support is being seen in prices..," Oswal's Agarwal said.

"Looking at the market breadth, it is quite likely that the index might touch the 3,600 mark." On Friday, the BSE's 30-share index rallied to 3,443.56--the intra-day high but ended with a net gain of 53.78 points at a provisional 3,416.17.

Buying was focussed on pharmaceutical and consumer non-durable stocks, dealers said. Foreign funds were keen buyers in Bajaj Auto, Hind Lever, MTNL, Colgate, Tata Tea, Castrol, Glaxo and Procter & Gamble.
Bajaj Auto rose 39.0 rupees to 980.0, Colgate 9.25 to 255.50, Hindalco 23.75 to 745.0, ITC 16.0 to 346.0, MTNL 11.0 to 249.0, Tata Tea 8.50 to 229.75 and L&T 8.0 to 245.0.
SBI, however lost 1.25 rupees to 253.75, TISCO 3.50 to 185.50 and Reliance 1.0 to 221.0. The National Stock Exchange index advanced 22.85 points to 979.45 provisional close.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
